[[File:Dactyloctenium aegyptium (L.) Willd.tif|thumb|'''Dactyloctenium aegyptium''' (L.) Willd.]]
'''''Dactyloctenium aegyptium''''', or '''Egyptian crowfoot grass''' is a member of the family [[Poaceae]] native to Africa and Asia.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dactyloctenium aegyptium (L.) Willd. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:397387-1 |access-date=2024-01-06 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref> The plant mostly grows in heavy soils at damp sites.

==Description== 
[[File:Dactyloctenium aegyptium at Peradeniya Royal Botanical Garden.jpg|right|thumb|at Peradeniya Royal Botanical Garden]]

This grass creeps and has a straight shoot which are usually about 30 centimeters tall.<ref>{{cite book |author=National Research Council |title=Lost Crops of Africa: Volume I: Grains |url=http://books.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=2305 |access-date=2008-08-01 |volume=1 |date=1996-02-14 |publisher=National Academies Press |isbn=978-0-309-04990-0 |pages=267 |chapter=Wild Grains |chapter-url=http://books.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=2305&page=251 }}</ref>

==Food==
''Dactyloctenium aegyptium'' is still a traditional food plant used as a [[famine food]] in [[Africa]], this little-known grain has potential to improve nutrition, boost food security, foster rural development and support sustainable landcare.{{Citation needed|date=March 2010}}

==Invasive species==
In other areas of the world, including parts of the United States, the grass is considered a weed and [[invasive species]].
